chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Lester Young's rehearsal band and the Hammond booking dispute
summary: Prez rehearsed a band at the Woodside; when he learned John Hammond would book him only as Billie Holiday's band, he dropped it.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I think they probably had a few thousand and didn't follow up on it. I don't think it made any difference to them, you know. But we had a very good little band at this time. It was Prez, Clyde Hart, Doc West, and Shad Collins. It was a good band. And we recorded with Billie, but John Hammond at this time wanted to do something for Prez, you know. He had left Basie, and we were rehearsed at the Woodside for quite a while. But he wouldn't use a piano, you know, he would just use guitar and bass and drums. And at this time I was playing checkers with Clyde Hart every night, you know. He thought he was a great checker player, and I'd go to his house every night.

But I got him to come by our rehearsal, and just made Prez use him. And Prez loved him so we started using piano at this time. But originally it was just guitar, but now why Prez was forming this band was because John Hammond told him that he was going to book him, but Prez found out that John Hammond was only going to book him if he would work -- I think Billie was going to be Billie Holiday's band.
And when Prez found this out, you know, he was very proud, you know, and when he found this out he just chucked the whole thing. And so consequently, we did very little work.
Well, he and (inaudible), Billie were very close.

That had nothing to do with the way they felt about eachother. They loved eachother. But Prez was Prez, and Lady was Lady, you know. So when he found out this was happening he just blew the whole thing up.
